finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes the attacker-supplied `state` parameter to Marshal.load after Base64 decoding. This is insecure deserialization and allows remote code execution through a Ruby gadget chain, such as Gem::Requirement or ERB-based universal gadgets.
finding.source: HTTP POST /restore form parameter `state` (params[:state]), attacker-controlled and public ingress (Sinatra default listener)

trace.note: Route `post "/restore"` is publicly reachable with no authentication filter
params[:state] is Base64-decoded without any integrity check (no HMAC or signature)
The decoded bytes go straight into Marshal.load, which instantiates arbitrary objects and can trigger gadget chains
state.inspect returns the result to the caller, which also leaks object contents

finding.guards_checked: Checked for authentication, before filters, a signature or HMAC on the payload, a class allowlist, and the use of safe formats such as JSON. None exist. The file is only 17 lines, has no middleware or Rack::Protection bypass relevant to deserialization, and CSRF protection does not matter for a direct attacker request.

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) from the unauthenticated POST /restore route (app.rb:5) directly into Marshal.load, with no auth, signature, or class allowlist anywhere in the 17-line file, and app.rb:7 returns state.inspect to the caller.
